newsitem.title: INDIA: One killed in grenade blast outside Kashmir shrine.
newsitem.headline: One killed in grenade blast outside Kashmir shrine.

text.p: A grenade exploded outside Kashmir's holiest Moslem shrine on Friday, killing one person and wounding five, police said.
They said unidentified militants hurled the grenade at a bus stop outside the Hazratbal shrine on the outskirts of Srinagar, the summer capital of India's Jammu and Kashmir state.
More than 25,000 Kashmiri Moslems were gathered at the shrine for Friday prayers when the blast occurred at 12:50 p.m. (0720 GMT), police said.
"Six persons were injured in the grenade explosion and later one died in the hospital," a police spokesman said.
The shrine, on the bank of the Kashmir Valley's famous Dal Lake, houses what is believed to be a hair from the beard of Islam's Prophet Mohammad.
In a separate attack, suspected guerrillas lobbed another grenade at a paramilitary patrol in Shopian town, 51 km (31 miles) south of Srinagar, police said.
They said the grenade did not explode and was later neutralised by local police.

More than a dozen militant groups are fighting a separatist rebellion in Kashmir for either independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan. Police and hospitals say at least 20,000 people have been killed since the revolt erupted in 1990.
